card: Adds a weekly CI job to monitor the expiration date of the Windows code-signing certificate and automatically open an issue 90 days in advance. Currently, maintainers rely on release candidates to discover expired certificates, which risks delaying urgent or out-of-band point releases. The author notes that relying on regular release cycles is insufficient for short-notice bugfix releases.
evidence: PR description: 'We have previously "relied on Release Candidates" as a dry-run for codesigners to realise that a certificate has expired and have time to fix it. "Noticing during RC cycle" also might not be appropriate in the future if we release more bugfix minor/patch releases on short notice.'
problem: Bitcoin Core lacks automated monitoring for code-signing certificate expiration. Maintainers previously relied on release candidate cycles to discover expired certificates, risking delays during unscheduled minor or patch releases.

risk.why: Only adds a scheduled CI workflow; a failure would create noisy issues or fail a non-blocking check.

scope_notes: The patch adds a single CI workflow configuration file.
summary: Adds a weekly CI workflow to monitor the expiration date of the Windows release code-signing certificate. If the certificate is within 90 days of expiration, the job automatically opens a repository issue alerting maintainers.
uncertainties: Diff was not provided in context, though the commit message and PR description clearly define the workflow change.
